## Purpose

The pre-semester campaign shipped 21 items and, per the standing "log every out-of-scope find" rule, accumulated a large register of deferred/emergent findings plus a Phase-5 hygiene backlog. This campaign organizes **all outstanding work** into one prioritized picture so it can be worked down in an orderly fashion.

**Ordering principle (as requested):** each item is ranked **primarily by what it blocks** (delivery to editors/readers → biology onboarding → another finding → nothing), and **secondarily by severity** (correctness → robustness/hardening → polish). Tiers P0→P3 encode that ordering.

**A structural truth worth stating up front:** the highest-blocking items are **operational**, not code — nothing merged in items 12–21 is live to editors until the server is deployed, and no content fix reaches readers until vefur is synced. Those are **[LEAD]**-executed. The efni **[CODE]** backlog that I execute is a set of medium-severity themed batches (P1–P2) plus a long low/polish tail (P3).

## How to run

- **Per item:** brainstorm → writing-plans → subagent-driven-development, **one PR per item**. `npm test` from the repo root is the **authoritative gate** (no branch protection — a red PR can still merge, so local green is the real proof). Whole-branch adversarial review before each PR (the item-17/-21 pattern).
- **Legend:** **[CODE]** = I execute. **[LEAD]** = you execute (deploy / data-op / product decision). **[decision-gated]** = a **[CODE]** item blocked on an L7-style lead decision — resolve the decision first.
- **Register provenance:** codes like `I14-R2`, `MTA-R8`, `osd-1`, `P1-R1` are defined in the pre-semester campaign's register sections (`docs/plans/2026-07-11-pre-semester-coding-campaign.md`) and the SDD ledger. This doc consolidates and re-prioritizes them; it does not restate their full history.
- **Excluded false-positives:** the inventory sweep surfaced two register lines that are **already resolved** and are NOT in this campaign: **B4-D11** (fixed #279 + data #280 — biology term round-trip is live) and **I18-R1** (closed by item-19 #306 — tag-at-approval). Re-verify any code against its register line before starting; a line *describing* a fixed problem is not open work.
- **⚠️ This register was built from *summaries of itself*** (see Provenance below) and so **never carried the 2026-07-11 review's own findings**. The [closure audit](../audit/2026-07-26-closure-audit.md) recovered 8 of them — now **§C10**. That ledger is **frozen evidence**, not a second register. **Closing a C10 item = edit §C10 here. Do not edit the ledger.** One fact, one live home — see CLAUDE.md § *One source of truth*.

B is a stopgap that names its own successor; C is the real fix and is this item's implementation.**
  - 🔴 **WHY THIS ENTRY EXISTS AT ALL.** A version of this ruling was stated on 2026-08-15 and recorded **only** as a parenthetical inside §C80 — *"(The three dropped books are being removed from preview on namsbokasafn-vefur — vefur's work, not this repo's.)"* — plus a copy in the RESUME block wrapped in `*(Superseded 2026-08-15, retained: )*`. **Three defects in one sentence:** it is a **present-tense status claim that was false** (all five books were still live seven days later, 268/25/26/31/34 sitemap URLs); it **assigns the work to the wrong repo** (see the mechanic below); and it carries **no id, no owner, no status verb**. ▶ **A ruling parked inside a bullet marked `Superseded` is unreadable as status BY DESIGN** — which is why the register's own `▶ NEXT` pointer went on instructing a physics sync for four more days. → [[engineering-lessons]]
  - 🔴 **EFNI IS THE OPERATIVE SIDE, NOT VEFUR — MEASURED IN THE SISTER REPO'S CODE, NOT INFERRED.** `sync-content.js` derives `availableBooks` by `readdirSync`-ing **THIS** repo's `books/`, keeping any book with at least one `/^\d{2}$/` chapter dir under `05-publication/{mt-preview,faithful}/chapters/` — **existence only; contents are never inspected** — and its destination-deletion sweep is keyed on that list, **outside** the per-book loop. **Two consequences:** ① a vefur-side deletion is **silently undone by the next bare sync**; ② a sync **scoped to the two kept books removes NOTHING**, because `--delete` is scoped to `${bookDest}/` inside the loop and never visits a withdrawn book's destination. ⚠️ **The scoping form CLAUDE.md prescribes is the form that does not withdraw.**

- **C101 · ⚠️ SIX MORE LATENT EXTRACTION/INJECTION EDGE CASES FROM THE §C88 WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW, RECORDED HERE BECAUSE THEIR ONLY OTHER RECORD IS THE GITIGNORED SDD WORKSPACE THIS PLAN DELETES AT CLOSE-OUT** — **[CODE]** — **P3** — *found 2026-08-19 by the §C88 whole-branch review, mostly while re-deriving the mechanism behind kills R3, R5 and R7 rather than as new candidate findings.*
  - **This branch opened §C97** — the entry naming exactly this class, "a citation to a gitignored path is not evidence, it is a promise the repo cannot keep" — **and then left these six unlogged** in its own workspace. None is urgent; all six are cheap to lose permanently, which is the only reason this entry exists.
  - **① Sibling-`<list>` media double-capture in `orderedExerciseBlocks`** (`tools/cnxml-extract.js`, the bare-`<media>`-block collection loop). Its nesting check tests only against `paraSpans` (`nested = paraSpans.some(...)`), not list spans, so a `<media>` that is a sibling inside a `<list>` item — not inside a `<para>` — is never recognised as "nested" and is appended as its own top-level media block *in addition to* whatever `processList` captures for that item. **0 live occurrences measured**; if it ever fires, `dedupeAltSegments` Rule 1 (`tools/cnxml-extract.js:583-668`) splices the duplicate id out before any count runs, so today it is latent, not a live gap.
  - **② Self-closing `<media …/>` inside a `<para>` is unreachable by `extractInlineText`.** Its inline-media capture (`tools/cnxml-extract.js:246`) is `` /<media([^>]*)>([\s\S]*?)<\/media>/g `` — a **paired**-tag pattern only; a self-closing `<media … />` inside running prose text never matches it, so its alt (if any) is silently omitted from the extracted segment. Pre-existing (not introduced by this branch), **0 corpus occurrences measured**.
  - **③ A note's own inner `<para>` can duplicate as a top-level `example.content` para entry.** Same shallow-scan root cause as ①: the `paras` array a note-level strip is built from is a non-nested, top-level scan, so a para genuinely nested one level deeper is not excluded from a sibling structural walk that also reaches it. Pre-existing, **0 occurrences measured**.
  - **④ `stripContainersByLength`'s partially-overlapping-span hole.** Already documented in the function's own docstring (`tools/cnxml-extract.js:1572-1581`, function defined at `:1589`): `paras` comes from `extractElements`'s non-greedy `([\s\S]*?)</para>`, which truncates an outer `<para>` at the *first* inner `</para>` — so a para span and a list span can partially overlap (neither nests the other, neither is disjoint), and length-ordered stripping guarantees nothing for that case: whichever is stripped first can corrupt the other's `fullMatch`, leaving it in the residue as a silent no-op. The docstring was corrected during this branch; **0 corpus instances measured**; the code limitation it describes had no register line before this entry.
  - **⑤ `assertNoDroppedListBlocks`'s `rendered` set can be joined by an alt-less media id, which can mask a genuine drop.** The guard's `walk()` helper (`tools/cnxml-extract.js`, inside `assertNoDroppedListBlocks`) does `rendered.add(n.id)` for *any* `{type:'media'}` structure node, whether or not it carries an alt segment — so the guard's evidence that an id "renders" is satisfied by bare structure-tree presence, not by confirmed emission. **Reachable only after some other strip has already failed** — a defense-in-depth gap in the safety net itself, not a live defect on its own.
  - **⑥ The missing container strip in `orderedExerciseBlocks`/`processTable`'s entry scan — an asymmetry with this branch's own two sibling emitters, which DO carry the strip.** This is the mechanism behind refuted findings R3 and R5: **258 physics + 13 microbiology = 271** duplicate-emit segments would result if it fired for real. It would not ship silently: R3 established that a genuine shear produces a new maximum `auto-N` id absent from any prior translation file, which `getSeg` records as a miss, which flips `report.complete` to `false` and makes the CLI refuse the module (`--allow-incomplete` defaults false and is passed by nothing in `tools/`, `scripts/`, `server/` or `.github/`) — and R5's structure-level duplicate (per-figure DOM census: chemistry 115, physics 113, microbiology 85, biology 189) is inert in every traced consumer (`collectMediaAlts` is idempotent; `applyMediaAltDom` never iterates `element.content`; `buildExample`'s `stripTags` doesn't list `media`). **Inert today; the asymmetry itself is the thing worth a line** — the sibling emitters were given the strip deliberately and these two were not.

- **C96 · ⚠️ PUBLISHED HTML IS NOT BYTE-REPRODUCIBLE ACROSS RENDERS — MathJax id counters differ per render pass** — **[CODE]** — **P3** — *found 2026-08-18 during §C9 Task 5's real ch10 render, while distinguishing renderer drift from the intended fix.*
  - MathJax emits per-render SVG id counters (`id="MJX-6-…"` vs `id="MJX-35-…"`) whose starting value depends on how many modules were rendered earlier in the same pass; the glyph path data after the id is byte-identical. Measured on ch10's `10-answer-key.html` and `10-key-equations.html`: **9 changed line-pairs, all 9 byte-identical after normalising the `MJX-\d+-` prefix.**
  - ▶ **Consequence: a `git diff` after a re-render can never be read as "nothing changed."** Any future "did the re-render alter anything?" check must normalise that prefix before comparing — otherwise a harmless re-render reads as a content regression, or a real regression hides inside a page of expected-looking id churn.
  - `cnxml-render.js` already imports `resetMathJaxIds` from `tools/lib/mathjax-render.js`, so the fix may be small — **unverified; not investigated as part of §C9.**
  - *[severity: makes render diffs unreadable without normalisation, no reader-facing effect · reader-visible: no · blocks: nothing · relates: §C9]*

- **C89 · 🔴🔴 §C81's FIGURE ALT TRANSLATIONS ARE EXTRACTED, PAID FOR, AND THEN DISCARDED AT INJECT — 627 of 951 (65.9%) ON MERGED `main`, PRESENT TENSE** — **[CODE]** — **P1, ahead of every other §C82 item** — *found 2026-08-16 by the §C88 design exploration, which was chartered to answer a different question entirely; independently reproduced by the controller with a from-scratch sentinel probe before being recorded.*
  - 🔴 **MEASURED, TWICE, INDEPENDENTLY. Method: extract each chemistry module, overwrite every `:alt:` segment's TEXT with a unique sentinel token, run the real `buildCnxml`, count tokens in the output.**

    | | chemistry, 149 modules |
    |---|---|
    | alt segments emitted | **951** |
    | translations that REACH the injected output | **324** |
    | **discarded** | **627 — 65.9%, across 130 of 149 modules** |

    ✅ **The 324 survivors ARE the positive control**: they are exactly the in-`<para>` (214) and standalone (110) positions, at ~100%. **The instrument is not broken — the figure path is.** The exploration's independent run gave 626/214/110 against the controller's 627/324; the one-element difference is a boundary case, not a disagreement about the mechanism.
  - 🔬 **CAUSE, read from source.** `buildFigure`'s id-bearing path (`tools/cnxml-inject.js` ~2354–2390) sets `figureCnxml = match[0]` — the **verbatim original figure block, English `alt` and all** — then swaps only `<image src>` and `<caption>` and returns it. `readAlt(element.media.alt, getSeg)` appears **only in the fallback branch** (~:2403), reached solely when the figure has no id or no source match. **A second instance:** `~:1249` calls `readAlt(media.alt)` with **no `getSeg` argument at all**, so by `readAlt`'s own contract it can only ever return `alt.text` — the extraction-captured English.
  - 🔴 **WHY EVERY GATE ON THIS BRANCH IS BLIND TO IT, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT GENERALISES.** The English `alt` is still present in the output — only *untranslated*. So the attribute COUNT is unchanged, and **every count-based check reports clean**: §C82 Plan A's round-trip check, `cnxml-extract-alt-corpus`, and E5's coverage check all pass. ▶ **This is §C85's documented "counts attributes, not content" boundary firing in production, and it is not hypothetical — that boundary is currently masking a 100% failure of the figure path.** The round-trip docstring warns of a *hypothetical future* seg-id divergence; **this is a different and worse mechanism — the preserved path looks up no segment id at all.**
  - 💰 **IT IS A LIVE SPEND DEFECT, not only a quality one.** The figure position is the majority of chemistry's alt characters, so re-MT'ing chemistry today buys translations for ~⅔ of its alt text and throws them away. ⚠️ **The exploration puts the wasted portion at ~519,714 chars ≈ 5,197 ISK; treat that as indicative and RE-DERIVE it** — §C81's own budget line is already recorded as needing re-derivation rather than scaling.
  - ▶ **CONSEQUENCE FOR §C88, and it inverts that item's design:** all five positions §C88 targets live in **preserved-verbatim subtrees** (`buildExampleDom`, `buildExerciseDom`, `buildNoteDom`, `buildTable`'s verbatim `entryMatch`), none of which routes through the two builders the sentinel proved actually write a translated alt. **Adding §C88's emitters first would produce 197 MORE extracted, MT'd and discarded segments.** ▶ **Write-back for preserved subtrees must land BEFORE any new emitter — and the same mechanism repairs these 627.** §C88 is therefore **blocked by §C89**.
  - ⚠️ **A hazard the fix must not walk into:** `buildExampleDom` calls `deduplicateMedia`, which keeps the **FIRST** `<media>` by id — so a newly-built translated copy appended after the preserved English one is **silently deleted**. That is byte-for-byte the §C81 Critical's shape.
  - ▶ **ACCEPTANCE GATE IS ALREADY DESIGNED, because the finding came with its instrument: the sentinel test.** A count-based check cannot gate this by construction; the gate must overwrite segment text with a distinguishable token and assert it reaches the output. **Its positive control is built in** — the in-para and standalone positions must stay at ~100% while the figure position rises.

- **C78 · 🔴 A WRONG TERM CANNOT BE FLIPPED ACROSS A BOOK — PROPAGATION IS *SEGMENT*-KEYED, NOT *TERM*-KEYED — AND THAT IS WHAT SETS THE PRICE OF EVERY GLOSSARY ERROR** — **[LEAD]/[CODE]** — **P1** — *found 2026-08-12 from a [LEAD] framing question. **The framing is the durable part and is recorded first, because it is the decision rule the glossary items turn on.***
  - 📐 **THE [LEAD]'s RULE, AS STATED.** A wrong translation across a whole book is **(a) unacceptable** if fixing it requires manually changing every occurrence or a re-MT (time and/or money); **(b) acceptable** if the editor's glossary system allows a single *flip* of a term that propagates at least **semi**-automatically through the book.
  - 🔴 **MEASURED ANSWER: WE ARE IN (a).**
  - **`propagationService` exists and is the only cross-module write in the editor stack — but it keys on the SEGMENT, not the term.** `findOccurrences` skips anything where `concordance.normalizeEn(seg.en) !== enNorm`: **normalized-exact ENGLISH match**. It answers *"apply my translation of this exact sentence everywhere that sentence recurs."* ▶ **A wrong term's occurrences sit inside thousands of DIFFERENT sentences, so exact-EN matching never groups them.**
  - ✅ **THE EXPENSIVE PARTS ARE ALREADY BUILT, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THIS ENTRY:** a cross-module write path with per-occurrence `eligible`/`already-matches`/`conflict` classification · pending-edit semantics with no auto-approve and no auto-publish · a structural-marker guard (`sourceEn` is a **required** parameter precisely so it cannot be disarmed) · and the reader path (`applyApprovedEdits` → faithful → inject → render). **Per-term occurrence reporting exists too** — `buildModuleTerminologyReport` returns `{english, expected, count, segments[]}` — **scoped per module, though the matcher beneath it is not.**
  - ❌ **WHAT IS MISSING IS ONE THING, AND IT IS THE HARD ONE: generating the correct INFLECTED TARGET form.** Replacing `frumeindanna` with `atómanna` is morphological *generation*. `buildInflectionRegex` uses `inflections` to **MATCH**; matching a source form does not tell you what to write. Inflections are populated on ~27,728 of 92,303 Icelandic terms. ▶ **The editorial way round it is already on record** — [`docs/decisions/2026-08-12-matecat-evaluation-and-editor-architecture.md`](../decisions/2026-08-12-matecat-evaluation-and-editor-architecture.md) carries forward *"a per-term list of acceptable TARGET forms, which is editorial and needs no morphology"*. **That converts generation into validation — enough for *semi*-automatic, which is the [LEAD]'s stated threshold.** ⚠️ And read [[compounder-sizing]] before proposing morphology tooling.
  - 🔴 **THE STRATEGIC CONSEQUENCE — A FLIP IS A SUBSTITUTE FOR GLOSSARY PERFECTION, NOT A COMPLEMENT TO IT.** Perfecting the glossary is unbounded work against homographs, domain drift and Íðorðabankinn's own self-inconsistency, with a feedback loop that **only ever fires when a domain expert happens to read the right word** — §C73 and §C77 were each found exactly that way, one by the [LEAD] reading one word and one by reading one diff. **A flip makes every FUTURE error cheap, including the ones nobody has found**, and is needed regardless because editorial preferences change over a textbook's life. ▶ **It is the option that does not have to be right the first time.**
  - ⚠️ **A NEAR-MISS WORTH KEEPING: the first pass concluded "no bulk write path exists" and was about to be logged.** A grep carrying a positive control found `propagationService` immediately. **The absence was TRUE for term flips and FALSE for segment propagation, and only the measurement separated the two** — an absence stated one level too broadly reads exactly like a finding.

'[[lb:]]' : '[[rb:]]')` — **1:1, stateless, no pairing logic**. The check is `git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD`, network-free because a successful push updates the remote-tracking ref; an indeterminate count fails loud — the inversion the off-box DB backup already used. `GET /api/health` gained `checks.content_backup` (`server/lib/contentBackupHealth.js`, threshold `CONTENT_BACKUP_STALE_HOURS`, default 6h) which gates `allOk`, and `scripts/deploy.sh` now **prints** the health verdict it used to discard — nothing else polls that endpoint, so this is where a human sees it, and the readout names the not-ok checks so a stale content backup is distinguishable from the ambient off-box `degraded`. Each rebase mints a new hash for the same content. **So "search dev's history for that sha" is structurally guaranteed to fail, and its age is invisible from `git log --oneline`** — only the author-vs-committer date gap reveals it. *This is the diagnostic to reach for; a hash lookup is not.*

It printed the answer I expected. The two accompanying `git show 2c8da016:…` greps returned `0` for the same reason. **A ref that does not resolve makes an ancestry check and a `grep -c` both fail *open*, looking like a clean negative result.** Verify against a ref you have confirmed resolves — and note this is the same class as `[[engineering-lessons]]`'s vacuous-pass entries, met on prod-only hashes rather than in a test.

  - **The arc, all five rounds (the block above records round 1 only).** Five whole-branch adversarial reviews ran on this branch before the PR opened, each fixing what the previous one found and each finding some of its own fixes wrong: **confirmed findings 8 → 5 → 6 → 2 → 0; worst severity CRITICAL → CRITICAL → important → important → none.** Round 1 is detailed above (the inert shrink guard). Round 2 (5 confirmed, 1 CRITICAL): `parseArgs`'s `if`/`else if` chain had no final `else`, so `--book=<slug>`, a bare positional, or a typo like `--books` silently meant "every book" while `--force` still applied — round 1 had closed only the bare-`--book` instance, not the class; plus the shrink-guard's own test fixtures were degenerate (`approved(n)` always had `total === approved`), so a mutation check showed the approved clause could be deleted with the suite still green. Round 3 (6 confirmed, 1 important, 0 critical): round 1's own fix (tolerant `countTerms`/`countApproved`) had silently turned a fail-loud crash on a malformed `exportFn` return into a **silent bad write** — exit 0, heartbeat green, an empty glossary committed; fixed with a shape guard ahead of any comparison. Round 4 (2 confirmed, both important, 0 minor — first round with no critical or minor survivors): `--book ''` parsed as present-but-falsy, so `parseArgs` and `runGlossaryExport` disagreed on what counted as "no book" and an empty value silently widened to every glossary at once; and the refusal/dry-run/success messages' total-term pair was unpinned by any test (every fixture in the file happened to have `total === approved`). Round 5: 0 confirmed — the branch's code was clean, but reading the raw findings (not just the verdict) caught one its own verifiers had wrongly refuted: the implementation plan (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-c14-glossary-export-runner.md`) still showed round 1's CRITICAL approved-only `shrinkVerdict` verbatim in its Task 3 code fence — accurate as history, dangerous as a rebuild recipe, since this repo's workflow is plan → TDD.   - **Most findings in each round were introduced by the previous round's own fix**, not pre-existing — the same "review the branch, not just the original problem" lesson C10 taught. Two defect classes each recurred (the branch's own commits call out the third-and-onward recurrence explicitly rather than treating it as a fresh finding):
    - **(a) producer/consumer predicate mismatch** — a guard checked a value was *present* while its consumer checked it was *truthy*. Round 1's `--book` fix checked `!== undefined`; `runGlossaryExport` checked truthiness. `--book ''` is present-and-non-undefined (passes the first check) but falsy (fails the second), so an empty value slipped through the seam and silently widened scope to every glossary-bearing book, with `--force` on the same command line bypassing the shrink guard on all of them. Fixed by making both sides agree on an explicit `book === null` check, and by having `parseArgs` reject an empty/whitespace value outright.

The status file records **`since` per book** (when its *current* outcome was first observed, carried forward while unchanged), and `/api/health` goes **not-ok** once any book has been refusing longer than **`GLOSSARY_REFUSAL_STALE_DAYS` (default 7)**. **Why it was needed:** D2's insight stands — a refusal is not an error, and a permanently-red check gets tuned out — but every committed glossary is `merge-glossary`, so **the first cron run after this ships refuses every book that has one** *(corrected 2026-08-05 from "EVERY book" — see the correction bullet under this block's opening caveat; a book with an `absent` baseline is not refused, it is WRITTEN, both gates inert)*, and under plain D2 that steady state reads `ok` **indefinitely**, with evidence only in a gitignored log. A refusal must not be allowed to become a permanent *silent* state. Reuses the repo's existing staleness doctrine (`content_backup`, `offbox_backup`).
    - **✅ D6's clock survives a transient error — FIXED 2026-08-05 in the whole-branch fix wave (both reviewers, independently; human-ruled).** `withSince` carried `since` only when the outcome **string** was identical, and all five `fail()` sites record `outcome:'error'` — so **one** erroring run in the middle of a refusal streak restarted the seven days. At the 2-hourly cadence that is not a corner case: `git-backup.sh`'s own comment predicts the error class (the export opens `sessions.db` as a **second** process while the live editorial server holds it). Demonstrated: refusing from day 0, one `SQLITE_BUSY` on day 6 → on day 8 `findStaleRefusals` returned `[]` for a book that had not exported in eight days, and **any** error recurring more often than weekly suppressed D6 **indefinitely**. `since` is now carried when the previous and current outcomes are **both unresolved** (`error` or any `refused-*`), so an error interlude neither manufactures a streak nor resets one and the alarm means *"not successfully exported since X"*. A **resolved** outcome (`wrote`/`adopted`/`unchanged`) still resets it, and `wrote → error` still resets, so the rule stays symmetric. The load-bearing new test asserts the **consequence** through the real health lib — `stale_refusals` must still contain the book on day 8 — not merely the intermediate `since` value.
    - **🆕 RULING — option (c), 2026-08-05: a filtered (`--book`) run writes NO status file, and there is no `filtered` field.** The first draft let a `--book` run overwrite the whole-corpus map, so the next unfiltered run found no previous entry for the untouched books and **reset their stale-refusal clocks**. That reset is **correlated with the alarm's firing window** — a lead hand-runs `--book <slug> --adopt` precisely *while the other books are still refusing and their clocks are running* — so it lands preferentially on the runs that matter. Option (c) makes the status file exactly parallel to the heartbeat: both whole-corpus, both withheld on a filtered run, **one rule instead of two**. The `filtered` field was **deleted rather than left permanently false** (a dead field implying filtered runs write is worse than no field). **Accepted, documented cost:** after `--book --adopt` the status file shows the stale outcome for ≤2 h — harmless, because it can only *delay* an alarm, never manufacture one.

The per-book map's **`detail` can embed `err.message` verbatim, including absolute server filesystem paths** (`EACCES … open '/srv/.../glossary-unified.json'`). Health now projects each book down to **`{outcome, since}`** via an allowlist **in `server/lib/glossaryExportHealth.js`, not in the route** — so a future second caller gets the projection for free instead of re-leaking by omission — and the projection **fails closed** (a non-object entry becomes `null`, never a passthrough). `detail` stays in the gitignored status file on the box.

    - **Lessons worth keeping (all cost real review time on this branch):**
      - **A controller's enumeration in a brief is not reliable — it under-counted twice on one task**, and the implementer caught both (a "four sites" table that had five; "three contract-changing tests" that were six). **Briefs should say "find all N and report the count", never enumerate.**
      - **A wrong number propagates faithfully through every derived document.** A term total was wrong in the design, and was transcribed unchanged into the plan → the task brief → a source comment → a commit message. **No assertion could have caught it**: the tests compute counts from disk and never hard-code a total — which is *why* they were right and the prose was wrong. Fixed **forward**, not amended, so the record shows the correction.
      - **A replacement for a vacuous test can itself be vacuous.** One rewrite used an empty `terms` array and passed either way; only running the mutation caught it. **Re-run the mutation against the NEW test, not just the old one.**
      - **The controller was wrong and the implementer right on a health-semantics claim**, confirmed in source by the reviewer: the justification for writing the status file before the error return is the `errors > 0` path (a persistently erroring exporter shows a **fresh `ran` beside a growing `age_hours`** — "running and failing" vs "cron stopped"), *not* the empty-book-list path, which returns above both writes.
      - **`npm run format:check` globs only `tools/**/*.js` and `scripts/**/*.js`** — so it matches **no `.mjs` file anywhere and nothing under `server/` at all**, and prettier drift in those trees is invisible to CI. **A clean `format:check` is not whole-tree evidence.** (The `server/` tree is still formatted, but by the lint-staged pre-commit hook, which only sees *staged* files — so a `server/` file changed outside a commit is checked by nothing.)

Surfaced while retiring the `chemistry-reader-tags` skill: the CNXML migration removed the *tools* of the Markdown-and-`:::`-directives era but left **consumers of that era still on live code paths**, operating on current data under retired assumptions. **This is deliberately NOT filed as dead code (item 22).** Dead code is unreachable and therefore harmless; the artifacts below are *reachable*, and two of them can produce a wrong or empty result **while every test stays green**. That is a correctness class, which is why this is P1 and item 22 is P3.
  - **The triage axis — one question per artifact: *can this silently produce a wrong result on current data?*** That, not "is it still referenced", is what should order the work. Applying it to what has been found so far:
  - **(a) ⚠️ HIGHEST — `hasApiMarkers` in `tools/cnxml-inject.js:1250` infers a segment's ERA from its own translated text, and it is the DEFAULT path.** It regex-sniffs for marker shapes to decide whether a segment is API-era; when false, three blocks of Markdown-era converters fire (`*text*`→italics, `~text~`→sub, `^text^`→sup, `~*t*~`→sub+emphasis, at `:1420`/`:1481`/`:1553`). The code comment states the reason plainly — those converters "would create false-positive markup from translated content (chemical formulas, etc.)" — i.e. **this guard is live code written to stop stale code from corrupting current data.** Measured over `02-mt-output` (30,932 segments): **22,163 (71.7%) have `hasApiMarkers` = FALSE**, because ordinary prose carries no inline markers, so the legacy path is the *majority* path, not an edge case; **139 of those (0.45% of all segments) also contain text matching a legacy shape** and are the concrete inspection list (approximate — the shape regex will have false positives; it is a starting set, not a defect count).
    - **⚠️ This is the SAME defect class the project already banned.** CLAUDE.md § *Extract-Inject-Render* carries the C13 durable rule (adopted 2026-07-27): *never decide inject behaviour from translated text, because **every segment is independently editable** and the test silently stops matching the first time an editor revises one side — with the whole suite still green.* `hasApiMarkers` does exactly that: an editor deleting the last `[[i:]]` from a segment flips it from "API-era" to "legacy-era" and silently arms the Markdown converters on modern text.
    - **⚠️ LIVE, NOT LATENT — inject has already run over every affected module.** *(🔴 **The module list in this paragraph was FALSIFIED 2026-08-07 and is kept as the original claim.** Measured by actual converter firing rather than shape match: **10 modules**, not 9. `ch03/m68700`, `ch09/m68750` and `ch17/m68825` **never fire**; `ch01/m68670` (4 segments), `liffraedi-2e ch03/m66440`, `orverufraedi ch01/m58782` and `ch05/m58805` **do** and are absent below. Per-module counts also differ: 62/39/24/9/16, not 61/36/24/5/3. → §C16's audit block.)* All **9** real modules holding a legacy-shape segment have `03-translated/` output. Concentrated in chemistry ch01: `m68674` (61 segments), `m68683` (36), `m68690` (24), `m68664` (5), `m68667` (3), then singles in ch03 `m68700`, ch08 `m68747`, ch09 `m68750`, ch17 `m68825` (plus 5 in `__e2e-fixture__`). **This is the audit's starting set.** ⚠️ Injected ≠ proven corrupted — a shape match is not a converter match, and the output may be benign; **verifying whether any produced wrong markup is task one**, and it is cheap because the module list is this short.

Both families are API-era, so this does not by itself prove two *eras* coexist in one module — but it does mean **a per-module property cannot be assumed**, and a per-module oracle may be unable to answer a per-segment question. **Establish which case holds BEFORE designing the fix**; the C1d note above is the standing warning that a register's fix *design* can be wrong while its root cause is right.

  - **Confirmed, not inferred.** `server/node_modules/archiver/package.json` is `"version": "8.0.0"`, `"type": "module"`, `"exports": "./index.js"`, and its namespace exports **classes, not a factory**: `{ Archiver, JsonArchive, TarArchive, ZipArchive }`. Under Node 22's `require(ESM)` support, `server/routes/books.js:14`'s `const archiver = require('archiver')` therefore binds an **object**, and `books.js:457`'s `archiver('zip', { zlib: { level: 9 } })` throws `TypeError: archiver is not a function`.   - **⚠️ THE SUITE IS GREEN ANYWAY, AND THAT IS THE FINDING.** `server/__tests__/books-routes.test.js` settles its promise inside a `res.setHeader` shim the moment `Content-Disposition` is set (`books.js:455`) — **two lines before the `archiver(...)` call**. So the appendices/numeric-chapter assertions genuinely pass, the route then explodes, and the `TypeError` surfaces only as an `ERROR: Download error` log line the runner does not fail on. The tests assert **zip *naming***; nothing asserts the zip is ever produced. *Textbook `[[engineering-lessons]]`: the dangerous check is the one that passes for the wrong reason.*
  - **Blast radius is one call site** — `require('archiver')` appears exactly once across `server/`, `tools/`, `scripts/`. Editor-facing (`requireAuth`), **not reader-facing**: nothing in the publication path uses it.
  - **⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-05 — this entry's own "the choice is not obvious" framing was WRONG, and the wrong half was the expensive one.** It claimed adopting v8 meant "a rewrite of the handler's archive block, not a one-line import change" because "the constructor/stream contract differs from the v7 factory". **Measured, not inferred: the contract does not differ.** `ZipArchive extends Archiver`, and `Archiver.prototype` still carries `file`, `directory`, `glob`, `append`, `finalize`, `abort`, `pointer`; the instance is still a Transform, so `.pipe(res)` works unchanged; `finalize()` still returns a promise. **The adopt was two lines** — the top-of-file `require` becomes `const { ZipArchive } = require('archiver')`, and the one construction in the download handler becomes `new ZipArchive({ zlib: { level: 9 } })` — with every other call in the handler untouched. *(No `file:line` here on purpose: the bullet above cites `books.js:14`/`:457` for the **pre-fix** tree, and this change itself moved both.)* *Recorded because the error is instructive and is the same shape as the #341 `npm view` mistake: an API-break severity was assumed from the release notes' "ESM-only, exports classes" rather than measured against the prototype.*
  - **Option (2) — pin back to `archiver@^7` — is dead, and staying on v8 is the reason.** Downgrading re-opens the `archiver → readdir-glob → minimatch → brace-expansion` advisory chain **#350 just bumped `overrides` for**, which would also walk straight into the standing trap that *an `overrides` pin can itself become the vulnerability*. (b) **`.file()` on a missing path emits `warning` (`ENOENT`), not `error`** — `finalize()` still resolves and nothing goes uncaught, so the adopt introduces **no new** need for an `archive.on('error')` listener and the handler's existing `fs.existsSync` guard keeps its meaning. *(Had it emitted `error`, an unhandled stream `'error'` would take the process down rather than the request — which is why this was checked before shipping.)* ⚠️ **Read that as a v7→v8 DELTA claim, which is what it is — not as "archive errors here are warn-only".** They are not: a file unlinked *after* the `existsSync`/`statSync` guard but *before* archiver's lazy read stream opens emits `error`, which the handler's `try/catch` does **not** catch, and that kills the process. That is **pre-existing and byte-identical under v7** — verified against the v7.0.1 tarball — so it is not this change's defect, but this change **makes it reachable again** by reviving a route that had been failing closed. Logged as **§C20**, which is the correct home for it.

Byte length + `PK` magic would not have been enough: an empty archive satisfies both. **Mutation-checked** — both new tests fail with the `TypeError` on unfixed `books.js` and pass after. The pre-existing `Content-Disposition`-settling block was **left intact**; it pins C1c appendices zip-naming and deleting it would have silently dropped that guard. Pinned: swapping `close`→`finish` fails every abort case in the suite.

The listener then never fired — no terminal line — while the already-armed watchdog still did, leaving a lone **`request still in flight`** warning with **no terminal partner**. That is exactly the signature the middleware documents as *"the process died mid-request"* (§C20), so an operator triaging a real hang would have been sent hunting a phantom one. **Measured against the real stack: 30 of 200 aborting requests — exactly 30 phantom warnings and 30 missing terminal lines, 1:1. The behaviour was right but **unpinned** — a mutation reading `req.path` late kept the whole suite green.

A close-time-only design logs nothing if the process dies mid-request — and **§C20 is a live P1 uncaught stream error that kills this exact process**, while C23's own incident included the unexplained 1,236 MB RSS spike. The `unref()` stops an in-flight request holding the event loop open through graceful shutdown.

Everything below is inside the measured window (cookie parsing, rate limiter, CORS, body parsing), so the number approximates what nginx measures rather than route time alone. Two measured consequences: a rate-limited **429 is now logged** (`RATE_LIMIT_MAX=3`, six requests → all six logged incl. three 429s; the old logger sat *below* the limiter and never saw one), and **static assets are still not logged** (`/css/common.css` → 200, no line), so log volume is unchanged.

The dominant cost is the **5.66 M executions of a `\p{L}\p{N}` lookbehind**, and per-exec cost degrades **~67×** with the number of distinct regexes V8 has *seen* — which neither caching, chunking (still 27.9 µs/exec at 200 live regexes) nor loop-reordering (only 2×) rescues.

Verified counterexample: forms `['mól','mól (m)']` against `mól (m)x` yields a **false "fannst ekki" QA warning**. Structurally unreachable on the English side (always one alternative) — safe there, unsafe on the Icelandic side.
      2. **Build the inflection regexes LAZILY, or AC merely RELOCATES the block.** They are constructed 28,903 times but executed ~313 times. Without laziness the AC cold build is a **6–11 s event-loop stall on every cache invalidation — i.e. on every terminology approval, an editor action.** With lazy `isRegex` the cold build is **under 1 s**.

An unsorted JSON diff will report spurious regressions; add `, h.id ASC` **first**, then capture the golden.

The heartbeat was last written at 20:00 by a healthy run; the 22:00 run failed to push and therefore (correctly, per C11(b)) did **not** rewrite it.   - **So the alarm is not broken — it is late, by up to 6 hours, on information it already holds.** C11(b)'s design principle is *"staleness is the alarm"*, which is right for the **silent** failure mode it was built for.   - **(a) Uncaught `error` → process exit. MEASURED, four scenarios, and the boundary is sharper than "a missing file".** The handler's `existsSync`/`statSync` guard does not close the window because `archive.file()` builds a **lazy** read stream. What decides the outcome is whether the failure lands **before or after archiver's own stat**:

    | Scenario | Outcome | Repeatability |
    |---|---|---|
    | unlink **immediately** after `.file()` (archiver's stat fails) | `warning ENOENT`, `finalize()` **resolves**, exit 0 — process survives | 6/6 |
    | unlink one tick later, **after** the stat (`setImmediate`) | **UNCAUGHT `ENOENT` → exit 1** | ⚠️ **1 of 6** — a genuine race with a narrow window |
    | `chmod 000` after `.file()` — stat succeeds, read denied | **UNCAUGHT `EACCES` → exit 1** | 6/6 — **the deterministic reproducer** |
    | an appended stream that errors mid-read | **UNCAUGHT → exit 1** | 3/3 |

    In every crashing case the handler's `try/catch` around `await archive.finalize()` **does not fire**: `_modulePipe` registers `_onModuleError` on the module *before* `finalize()` installs its reject listener, so `_onModuleError`'s `this.emit('error', err)` throws out of the module's `emit` and the rejection path never runs. ⚠️ **The first row is exactly the measurement §C19's fact (b) reports** — which is why both are true and why (b) must be read as scoped to that condition. ⚠️ **Use the `chmod` row to reproduce, not the unlink row** — unlink-after-stat crashed only 1 run in 6, so a fix "verified" against it will look green ~83% of the time on broken code. ⚠️ **Not hypothetical**: "Vista + Birta" rewrites `05-publication/` on the same box the download reads from, so a re-render concurrent with a download is a real trigger, not a contrived one.
  - **(b) Client disconnect leaks the request.** There is no `res.on('close')` → `archive.abort()`. An editor who cancels a large book download leaves the archiver writing into a dead socket and the handler promise pending.
  - **(c) The C19 test cannot see either.** It settles on the response stream's `end` or on `res.json`, so a mid-stream failure is outside what it observes. **Do not read C19's green as coverage of this.** A fix needs its own harness — one that injects a read failure mid-archive, which likely means making the file-enumeration seam injectable.
  - **🔴 THE OBVIOUS ONE-LINE FIX IS A TRAP — MEASURED 4/4, and this is the most useful thing in this entry.** Adding just `archive.on('error', …)` — the fix anyone would reach for — **does not fix it; it converts a crash into a hang.** With a listener attached and the deterministic `chmod` trigger: the listener fires with `EACCES`, and then **`finalize()` never settles** (still pending at 3 s) and **`res` is never ended**. So the process survives and the editor's browser instead holds an open chunked download that never completes and never errors, while the handler's promise and the `Archiver` leak for the process lifetime. A "fix" validated only by *"the server stopped crashing"* will ship exactly this.
  - **Shape of the fix (not prescribed — decide when taken):** the `error` handler must **also end the response** (destroy `res`) and stop waiting on `finalize()`, plus `res.on('close')` → `archive.abort()` for (b). ⚠️ A second constraint makes the reporting non-trivial: once `archive.pipe(res)` has written a byte, `res.headersSent` is **true** and the existing catch block's `res.status(500).json(...)` is already unreachable — so the handler cannot report a mid-stream failure to the client as JSON, only truncate. Whatever ships must decide what a half-written ZIP looks like to the editor. **Verify against the `chmod` reproducer and assert on *both* — no crash AND the response settles.** *[severity: robustness/availability — process-level · blocks: nothing]*
  - **✅ WHAT SHIPPED (2026-08-06, branch `fix/c20-download-stream-error`).** The handler races `finalize()` against a failure promise and never awaits `finalize()` unconditionally — *the race is the fix; awaiting finalize IS the hang.* On any failure it **destroys** `res` rather than ending it, and **aborts the archiver on every failure kind** (not only on disconnect). `res.on('close')` with a `writableFinished` guard is what detects a client disconnect. Spec/plan: [`spec`](../superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-c20-download-stream-error-design.md) · [`plan`](../superpowers/plans/2026-08-06-c20-download-stream-error.md). **Five tests in the new file, and all seven mutation rows measured red.** *(⚠️ This bullet said "**Four tests**, all mutation-verified" and "4 commits". Both were wrong: **three** tests were added in the first cut — the fourth counted was the pre-existing C19 test — and a commit count is stale the moment it is committed. **Do not put a commit count in prose**; `git log main..HEAD` is authoritative.)*
  - **⚠️ D1's RATIONALE was wrong; D1 itself is unchanged and better supported.** The claim that ending cleanly hands the editor "a truncated `.zip` that opens and is silently missing files" is **false** — a stream ended mid-archive has no end-of-central-directory record, so `unzip -t` reports *"cannot find zipfile directory"* and Python's `zipfile` raises `BadZipFile`. **The decision (destroy, not end) stands**: a saved file that cannot be opened at all is still worse than a transfer the browser flags as failed, because only the latter tells the editor to retry. This is a wording correction, **not** a reopening of the lead's decision.

The self-correction is worth more here than the corrected mechanism: **re-running a claim first-hand is not the same as re-running the RIGHT claim**, and this entry asserted the former while doing neither.

Measured: with the error listener attached and no race, the child **exits `0` in ~400 ms, silently**. `finalize()` genuinely never settles — so the report line never prints, which is *how* it is caught — but this harness has no listening socket holding the event loop open, so node drains and exits cleanly. **In production the socket does hold it open, which is why the same defect presents there as a request that hangs forever.** The assertion that catches the hang is the missing-`REPORT`-line check, which the spec had framed as a mere diagnostic.
    - **② The plan's client-disconnect test was VACUOUS and would have passed its own mutation.** As specified, T2 asserted only that the handler *settles* — which it does on the happy path regardless. Under the "delete `res.on('close')`" mutation it settled in 264 ms and stayed **green**. It was strengthened with `expect(res.destroyed).toBe(true)` (`res.emit('close')` does not set `destroyed`; only the handler's own `res.destroy()` does), and the mutation then turned it red. Its `setImmediate` was also dropped for a synchronous emit — the handler body has no `await` before `finalize()`, so deferring only raced compression.
    - **③ ⚠️ THE MOST GENERALISABLE RESULT — a mutation can be REAL and INVISIBLE, and the spec's prescribed disposition for that case would have written a FALSE claim into the source.** Removing the `writableFinished` guard turned **nothing** red across the entire **1852-test server suite**. The spec offered exactly two dispositions: *T3 red ⇒ load-bearing*, or *nothing red ⇒ defensive, downgrade the comment to say so*. **Neither was correct.** Probing `outcome` directly, **3/3 each way: without the guard a fully successful download resolves `{kind:'disconnect'}` and runs `archive.abort()` + `res.destroy()` against a completed response; with it, `outcome` is `null`.** Measured happy-path order is `finish → close(writableFinished=true) → handler returns`, so `close` arrives **while the handler is still awaiting the race**. The guard is **load-bearing**; the suite was simply blind to it, because the spurious abort lands after every existing observer has settled on `end` with complete, correct bytes. **A fourth test was added** — *"does not abort or destroy on a fully successful download"* — which spies `Archiver.prototype.abort` (⚠️ `abort` is **not** on `ZipArchive.prototype`; spying there misses it) and is red under that mutation. **Durable lesson: "no check went red" is not evidence the mutated line is optional. Distinguish *the change has no effect* from *no check can observe the effect* by probing the value directly before concluding either.**

- **C36 · Terminology concept model, Part A — SHIPPED, inert by construction; eight findings deferred to Part B/C, all load-bearing there** — **[CODE]** — **P1** — *logged 2026-08-08, merged to `main` as 17 commits and DEPLOYED the same day. Nothing reads the new tables and nothing was dropped. ⚠️ **The IMPORT ran against a throwaway copy — but migrations 045/046 DID apply to production's schema at that deploy**, because `migrationRunner` runs every migration's `up()` on every start. **Verified read-only on prod after the deploy:** all four tables present; `concept`, `concept_term` and `book_concept_preference` all **0 rows**; `book_domain_priority` **21 rows across all 6 registered books, none scoped to nothing**, orders matching `PRIORITIES` exactly; all four old terminology tables still present; `/api/health` `status: ok` with `migrations.total: 46`. That also closes the whole-branch review's stated gap — 046 had been measured only against a 5-book dev copy, never production's real `registered_books`. Part B cuts consumers over onto `concept`/`concept_term`; Part C drops the old tables. Evidence: [`test-results/concept-import-2026-08.md`](../../test-results/concept-import-2026-08.md). Finding 3 below cites **§C35** — same root cause, measured together.*
  1. **Re-import cascade-deletes editor term preferences.** `server/scripts/import-concepts.js:32` clears a concept's terms with `DELETE FROM concept_term WHERE concept_id = ?` then re-inserts with new autoincrement ids. `book_concept_preference.term_id REFERENCES concept_term(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` (migration 045), so re-importing a collection to pick up an Árnastofnun update **silently deletes every editor term preference for that collection's concepts** — no count, no warning in the returned stats. Twice-derived: measured directly, and found independently by a reviewer. Inert only because `book_concept_preference` is empty in Part A. **Must be resolved before Part B writes to that table.**
  2. **Migration 046 re-asserts the domain priority on every server boot, and the orphan case.** `server/services/migrationRunner.js` calls every migration's `up()` unconditionally on every start (no applied-migrations gate for the modern pattern), so `INSERT OR REPLACE` in `046-seed-domain-priority.js` is repeated *enforcement*, not a one-time seed. Two consequences, one root cause: (a) if Part B adds an admin control to reorder a book's domains, the next `systemctl restart` silently reverts it; (b) shortening a book's `PRIORITIES` list never deletes the orphaned rows, so a domain deliberately removed keeps its old `position` and keeps influencing every `ORDER BY position` consumer. Both fixed by `DELETE WHERE book_id = ?` before the insert loop, plus a decision on whether that table is user-writable.
  3. **`migration046.test.js`'s "a book scoped to nothing is the bug" test cannot detect that bug, and the bug is live on a fresh clone.** The test seeds `registered_books` with exactly the six slugs `PRIORITIES` contains, so the fixture *is* the map and the assertion is self-fulfilling. **Measured** on a database built by running all migrations against an empty file: only `lifraen-efnafraedi` and `edlisfraedi-2e` are registered, and both correctly received their priority rows (3 and 5). The other four do not exist at all — `019-register-new-books.js` registers `liffraedi-2e` and `orverufraedi` **without** the `NOT NULL` `registered_by` column that migration `003` declares, so `INSERT OR IGNORE` silently discards both (**§C35**), while `029-register-preview-books.js` registers its two *with* `registered_by: 'system'` and succeeds — the contrast is the tell; and **no migration registers `efnafraedi-2e` or `stjornufraedi` at all**, they reach `registered_books` only via the admin route. ⚠️ **Migration 046 is therefore NOT at fault and `if (!row) continue` behaves correctly** — every book that exists got its rows; on a fresh clone only 2 of the 6 books in `PRIORITIES` exist, so `resolve()` would scope four of them to nothing. Bounded by `migrationRunner`'s every-boot `up()`, which re-seeds them once they are registered through the admin route — **the same repeated execution that would silently revert an editorial reorder, so findings 2 and 3 are one coin and neither can be fixed without first deciding whether `book_domain_priority` is user-writable.** Needs a real-tree assertion, per spec §10.
  4. **Null and colliding `idordabanki_id`.** `importConcepts` only looks up an existing concept when `idordabankiId != null`, and SQLite permits multiple NULLs in a UNIQUE column, so a null-id entry re-inserts a duplicate concept on every run. Separately, two entries from different collections sharing an id silently overwrite, leaving one concept carrying both entries' terms. **Measured on the full 20-collection import: 0 null ids, and 70,187 concepts with 70,187 distinct `idordabanki_id` — zero collisions.** Neither is proof of uniqueness by construction; both are quantified as currently absent.
  5. **Domain vocabulary is triplicated with no shared constant and no test**: `COLLECTION_DOMAIN`'s values (`server/lib/conceptFromEntry.js`), `DOMAINS` (`server/scripts/verify-concept-import.js`), and `PRIORITIES`'s domains (`server/migrations/046-seed-domain-priority.js`). Measured clean today — all seven priority domains resolve to a non-empty `concept.domain` — but nothing keeps it clean, and a typo'd domain yields a fallback level that matches nothing, silently.
  6. **Neither `run-concept-import.js` nor `verify-concept-import.js` has a CLI entry point** (`require.main === module`), unlike `server/scripts/export-terminology.js:978`. The evidence file says "re-measure rather than trusting these numbers later", but the driver that produced them is not in the repo.
  7. **`homographs-separated` is one oracle pair wide** (`fruma`/biology, `rafhlað`/physics). Contamination involving no measured pair passes silently. **Do not widen the oracle by inference** — `flokkur` was excluded on reasoning and the full corpus then confirmed it appears in biology (3), which would have false-fired. Widening requires measurement, not a guess.
  8. **`model-is-non-empty` is corpus-wide**, so a single collection yielding zero still passes. Per-collection yield is computed by `runImport` and *printed*, never gated. *[severity: correctness/data-integrity (all inert today) · blocks: Part B]*

Chemistry's export resolves **both to `nákvæmni`**. Measured on the corpus, six concepts carry the English `accuracy` and **five give `hittni` as the head form** (biology ×2, mathematics ×2, plus one biology concept ranking `nákvæmni` 1 / `hittni` 2); the sixth — **physics/EDLISFR — says `nákvæmni`**. Chemistry's chain is `1.chemistry → 2.physics → 3.biology`, chemistry has no `accuracy` concept at all, so **physics@2 decides and biology's `hittni` at position 3 never gets consulted**. `precision` resolves to `nákvæmni` from the same collection, correctly. The two collapse because one domain decides both.
      - **⚠️ THREE THINGS MAKE IT INVISIBLE, and they matter more than the single term.** ① **`alternatives` is EMPTY** — it is built from the *winning concept's* other Icelandic terms, and physics concept 2500 has only `nákvæmni`, so `hittni` appears nowhere in the exported entry. ② **The losing IN-SCOPE answers are not reported at all** — `resolve()` surfaces `outOfScope` (here: the two mathematics `hittni` concepts, badged) but a lower-position in-scope concept that loses the race vanishes silently. ③ **Árnastofnun's own data conflates them**: concept 6524 carries BOTH English terms on ONE concept, `nákvæmni` rank 1 / `hittni` rank 2.

The preference model chooses a **term within a concept**; **position still decides which concept wins**, so a preference on a position-3 concept can never beat position 2. **The model as built gives an editor no way to say "for this book, `accuracy` means `hittni`."** That is the gap B4 has to close, and it is not a UI question.

The answer is **migration 048 `book_term_preference (book_id, chapter, english, term_id)`** → see the **B4 block above**. **Nothing has shipped; §C38 closes when B4a merges.**

The plural triggers *perfectly*; a correct match emits no issue, so **nothing appears** — the panel is only visible when it disagrees. **Do not diagnose this class from which segments look quiet.** *(Not measured, and left open: whether the title HIGHLIGHT renders. - **C49 · ÍÐORÐABANKINN TERMS CARRY A RAW U+0001 WHERE AN ITALIC VARIABLE WAS LOST — `<i>␁</i>-adic` is *p-adic* with the letter gone** — **[CODE]** — **P2** — *logged 2026-08-11; surfaced by §C36 B4b-1 Task 7 when an assertion written to prove a separator byte safe went red on its first run.*
  - **Measured, with the counting unit stated because the two units differ**: **15 distinct EN strings / 24 distinct IS strings** contain a raw U+0001 (SOH); as **rows** that is **20 EN / 33 IS**. Independently re-derived by the controller on a fresh scratch-corpus build (70,187 concepts / 192,189 terms — reproduces the recorded control totals). ⚠️ The implementer reported 15/24 and the controller first measured 20/33; **they reconcile exactly as distinct-vs-rows**, not as a disagreement.
  - **Shape:** `"<i></i>"`, `"<i></i>-adic"`, `"<i></i> horn"`. The markup survived the import; the italicised **variable letter** did not. So these are **matchable EN automaton entries that can never match real text**, and the Icelandic ones are **unusable as editor-facing terms** — an editor offered `<i>␁</i> horn` sees markup and a control byte.
  - **This is an Íðorðabankinn IMPORT-FIDELITY defect, adjacent to §C36 B2's population but not covered by it.** B2 asserted row counts and it is right about them; nothing in that op inspected term *content* for control characters. **`verify-b4b1-gates.js` gate 4 now reports the count on every run**, so the number moves into view rather than needing re-derivation.
  - 🔴 **THE META-LESSON, which is a NEW VARIANT OF A KNOWN HAZARD AND EVADES THE EXISTING RULE.** CLAUDE.md § Commands warns that committed files contain **NUL** bytes and that plain `grep` reports *nothing* for strings they contain — the fix being `grep -a`. **U+0001 behaves differently and worse: it does NOT trip grep's binary heuristic at all.** `grep` matches normally; the byte simply **does not render**. Consequence, observed twice in one review cycle: the gate's source read as `join('')` and `split('')` to **both a reviewer and the controller**, when `cat -A` shows `join('^A')` / `split('^A')`. An Important finding was filed against a defect that did not exist, and its 3(b) half had to be **withdrawn on the implementer's byte-level evidence**. ⚠️ **`grep -a` does not help here — only `cat -A`, `hexdump`, or `od` do.** *(Candidate amendment to CLAUDE.md § Commands, deliberately NOT made unilaterally: that file is always-loaded and a durable-rule change belongs to the lead. ✅ **AUTHORISED AND MADE 2026-08-11, THEN MERGED ([PR #389](https://github.com/SigurdurVilhelmsson/namsbokasafn-efni/pull/389) → `main` `58956ea2`) AND CARRIED ON PROD'S CHECKOUT — "made" is not "merged" and neither is "deployed", and this entry now says which.** The amendment is in CLAUDE.md § Commands, beneath the NUL rule, and it was **re-measured before being written rather than relayed from this entry** — which sharpened it: a NUL makes grep **silent** (`exit 1`), a `U+0001` makes grep's **output lie** (matches, exit 0, and prints `alphabravo` for `alpha^Abravo`), so **`-a` is no defence and the reader is the one who is blind**. It also ships a census over **tracked** files, because the `--include` sweep the NUL rule uses returns 20 hits of which 15 are vendored `node_modules`/`.venv` noise; the tracked census returns four non-image files, and PNGs under `docs/` are a legitimate carve-out like `books/`.)*
  - **The gate's own separator was the trigger and is fixed**: `verify-b4b1-gates.js` no longer joins group members with any byte — it uses `JSON.stringify`/`JSON.parse`, which is injective by construction and holds no raw control characters. **The premise "no term can contain this separator" was false on this corpus**, which is exactly what the assertion added to prove it safe discovered.
  - *[severity: corpus data quality + a source-legibility hazard · blocks: nothing · no prod exposure — these strings match no real text]*

- **C48 · `c24-terms.json` IS SOUND AS A SPAN/ORDER INPUT AND IS NO LONGER TRUSTWORTHY AS A TIER INPUT — its synthesised subject tags were promoted from decoration to tier selectors by B4a's domain chain** — **[CODE]** — **P2** — *logged 2026-08-11 from §C36 B4b-1 Task 6, which hit it while porting the C24 golden to the concept model.*
  - **What changed underneath the fixture.** Before B4a the tier came from `book_subject_mapping` — **one** `primary_subject` per book, `chemistry` for efnafraedi-2e — so physics, biology **and** mathematics terms were all `fallback` **alike**, and a term's subject tag carried **no ordering information**. After B4a the tier comes from `book_domain_priority`, whose chain is `['chemistry','physics','biology']`, so **physics and biology are in scope and only mathematics falls back**. `findTermsInSegments`'s `hits.sort` keys on the in-scope/fallback partition **first**, so the tags now **select tiers**.
  - **The fixture was never built to carry that meaning, and in places its tags are chemically implausible**: `bomb calorimeter` → **mathematics**, `absolute zero` → **biology**, `atomic mass` tagged **chemistry *and* mathematics**. Harmless when everything non-chemistry was fallback alike; **load-bearing now**.
  - **Measured consequence on the golden, across all 24 segments** (scale stated: this is the 316-headword c24 fixture, **not** corpus scale): total match count **40 → 40, unchanged**; identical span **set** 21/24; identical span **list** 12/24; order-only differences 9/24; **genuinely different spans 3/24**. Two of the three hang directly on an implausible tag, so *that part of the diff is a synthesis artefact* — **but the mechanism is real** and fires in production wherever an out-of-chain multiword term overlaps a shorter in-chain one.
  - 🔴 **THE RULE THIS ESTABLISHES, and it reaches past Task 6:** **any gate, benchmark or test that reads a TIER, a `isFallback` badge, or an ISSUE COUNT off `c24-terms.json` is reading synthesised tags, not corpus truth.** §C36 B4b-1's **Task 7 (corpus gates)** and **Task 8 (bench)** both plan to use this fixture. Spans and order are still sound; tiers are not.
  - ⚠️ **A mapping that reproduces the golden byte-for-byte EXISTS and was deliberately REJECTED** — sending physics and biology to domains outside efnafraedi-2e's chain restores the old partition exactly. It is a mapping chosen to make an oracle pass, and it would **certify the cut-over against a fiction**. Named as considered-and-rejected in `seedC24Concepts.js`'s header so nobody re-discovers it as a clever fix. **Do not take it.**
  - **A design question falls out of this and is NOT settled** — *[decision needed]*: segment `m002:para:fs-id0012` now resolves `bomb calorimeter` (mathematics → fallback) → `calorimeter` (biology → in scope), i.e. **a shorter in-scope term beats a longer out-of-chain one**. That is **item 18's rule working exactly as written** (the book's own domain wins an overlap), and it may still be the wrong answer for a reader, because the longer term is the more specific one. **Tier priority vs longest-match specificity has never been decided on the merits** — it was inherited from the partition, not chosen. Whoever owns B4c should rule.
  - **Two further editor-visible measurements from the same tier change, unmeasured anywhere else** *(c24-fixture scale)*: the fixture's **issue count rose 5 → 22** (more terms in scope ⇒ more Icelandic-side checks run ⇒ more issues emitted), and **per-call regex compiles rose 11 → 56** (37 winner checks + 19 issue-path candidates). ⚠️ **The compile rise is NOT a §C24 relapse and the distinction is the whole point**: C24 existed because compiles scaled with **corpus size** (642 on this fixture pre-swap, ~28,903 in production); 56 scales with **match count**, and neither `loadEnglishEntries` nor `buildTermAutomaton` constructs a `RegExp` at all. Task 8 should still see the number.
  - **One more now-false rationale, same class as migration 044's.** `c24 fixture shape`'s first test — *"is fallback-heavy for a chemistry book"* — **still passes and its stated rationale is now false**: under the chain **244 of 326** translations are in scope and only the 82 mathematics ones fall back. It survives only because it measures the *chemistry share*, which the model change does not move. Annotated in place. *[severity: instrument trust · blocks: nothing, but Tasks 7 and 8 must read this first · no prod exposure]*

- **C47 · A CASE-HOMOGRAPH'S WINNER IS DECIDED BY IMPORT ORDER — `Am` (americium) vs `AM` (amplitude modulation) resolve to whichever `concept_term.id` is lower** — **[CODE]** — **P2** — *logged 2026-08-11 from a pre-census run while executing §C36 B4b-1; the mechanism is **pre-existing**, not introduced by the cut-over.*
  - **The mechanism, three identities that do not agree.** `conceptMatcher.loadEnglishEntries` groups **case-SENSITIVELY** (`GROUP BY text`; `concept_term.text` carries no `COLLATE`, so it is BINARY — migration 045), so `AC`, `Ac` and `ac` are **three** automaton entries. `termAutomaton.buildTermAutomaton` then **folds case** via `foldString`, so all three reach **one** keyword, and `byKeyword.get('ac')` returns all three ids. All three hits therefore claim the **same span**, and `findTermsInSegments`'s `consumed` tiler keeps whichever sorts first — after the `isFallback`/length keys tie, that is **`a.headwordId - b.headwordId`, i.e. the lowest `concept_term.id`**. Ids are assigned in **import order**. So the concept an editor is offered is decided by the order rows arrived in.
  - **Measured — 157 EN strings, and the collisions are SEMANTIC, not typographic.** Census run 2026-08-11 on a scratch corpus built from the raw Íðorðabankinn fetch (`~/idordabanki-raw-2026-08-07/`), which reproduced the recorded control totals (`concept` 70,187 · `concept_term` 192,189), so the build is sound. **157 distinct English strings collide under an ASCII lowercase fold; 15 do on the Icelandic side.** Samples: `AC,Ac,ac` · `AM,Am` · `OS,Os,os` · `Tropic of Cancer,tropic of cancer` — where `Ac` is actinium, `Am` americium, `AM` amplitude modulation, `Os` osmium. **Folding these manufactures ambiguity between genuinely different concepts**, which is the same hazard project memory records for BÍN's capitalised proper nouns case-folding onto ordinary words.
  - ⚠️ **NOT a B4b-1 regression, and the scope claim is bounded to what was measured.** The old model behaved identically — `terminology_headwords` was `UNIQUE(english, pos)`, so `AC` and `Ac` were separate headwords, ordered `LENGTH(h.english) DESC, h.id ASC` into the **same** `consumed` tiler. **What is NOT measured is whether the population grew**: 157 is a count over the *concept* corpus's 61,042 EN strings; the equivalent count over the old model's headwords was never taken, and this entry does not assert one.
  - **This is §C18's defect class** — an incidental ordering deciding an editorial answer — in a third location. Two instances were closed during B4b-1 execution (`outOfScope[0]`, and the intra-concept sibling memo whose staleness let *segment* order decide `alternative` vs `missing`); **this one is older than both and nothing pins it.** No test asserts which of a case-homograph group wins.
  - ⚠️ **DO NOT "FIX" THIS BY MAKING THE FOLDS AGREE.** `nocaseKey`'s ASCII-only behaviour must match SQLite's `COLLATE NOCASE` on `book_term_preference.english`; making it Unicode-aware **re-opens §C18**. Equally, grouping `loadEnglishEntries` case-insensitively would hand `conceptResolver.lookupCandidates` a string its `text = ?` lookup cannot find. The three identities are deliberate and documented in `conceptMatcher.js`; **the fix, if any, is a deterministic tie-break that is not an id** — e.g. prefer an exact-case match against the source span before falling back — not a normalisation.
  - **Bounded, deterministic, not flaky.** For a fixed database the winner is stable, so this does not cause CI flakes; it changes silently on **re-import, `VACUUM`, or an id-space change**. Reader exposure is **not** via this path — the matcher feeds the editor's terminology panel, while published substitution goes through the glossary export — so this is editorial-correctness, not reader-visible. *[severity: editorial correctness / silent-on-reimport · blocks: nothing · promote to P1 if an editor reports being offered the wrong element symbol]*
  - **Where the evidence lives:** the census recipe and both numbers are in the B4b-1 SDD ledger's "TASK 7 PRE-CENSUS" block; §C36 B4b-1's **gate 4** must therefore be written to **REPORT** the disagreement count with samples, not to assert the three folds agree — written as an assertion it fails on real data on day one.

- **C37 · ✅ FIXED 2026-08-08 — `main` was RED on the `audit` gate, and no commit caused it** — **[CODE]** — **P2** — *logged 2026-08-08 while checking PR #372's checks; the failure was on `main` too and predated that branch.* **Closed by `main` `664ec099`: `nanoid` 3.3.16 → 3.3.18. `main`'s CI is green — `Security Audit`, `Lint` and `Tests` all pass on that commit.**
  - **⚠️ THE PRESCRIBED FIX BELOW WAS NOT THE ONE USED, AND THE PRESCRIPTION WAS WRONG — read this before reaching for `overrides` on the next advisory.** The entry said "the fix is an `overrides` entry … add `"nanoid": ">=3.3.17"`". **No override was needed.** `postcss` requires `nanoid@^3.3.16`, and that caret range **already permits** 3.3.17 and 3.3.18 — nothing was pinning us to the vulnerable version except the lockfile's own recorded resolution, which `npm install` will not move. **`npm update nanoid` re-resolves within the range that was always allowed**, and the whole change is three lines (version, resolved, integrity). Adding an override would have created a permanent pin to maintain — and this entry's own next bullet warns that a pin can become the vulnerability. **Check whether the existing semver range already admits the fix before writing an override; here it did.**
  - **⚠️ AND THE DIAGNOSIS WAS DELAYED BY A CHECK THAT LIED IN THE REASSURING DIRECTION.** `npm ls nanoid` reported **3.3.18** — *newer* than the advisory's `<3.3.17`, i.e. safe — while `npm audit` reported the vulnerability. Both were right about different things: `node_modules` on disk had drifted to 3.3.18, and `package-lock.json` still pinned 3.3.16. **CI runs `npm ci`, so CI sees the lockfile — the only copy that matters.** Reading `npm ls` as the answer would have concluded the red was spurious. → the standing lesson in [[engineering-lessons]] about the right property and the wrong instrument.
  - **Verified against what `security.yml` ACTUALLY runs, which is four steps over BOTH trees**, not the one the failing log named: `npm ci` (root) · `npm ci` (server) · `npm audit --audit-level=high` (root) · same (server). All four green, reproduced in scratch directories holding only the two manifests — which is the `npm ci` path exactly, without a 1.9 GB checkout. The root tree now reports **zero vulnerabilities at any severity**, so nothing is queued below `high`; `server/`'s SheetJS CDN tarball still installs.
  - *Historical record of the entry as logged (its diagnosis of HOW the gate flipped stands; its prescription does not):* `npm audit --audit-level=high` on the **root** tree reports **1 high**: `nanoid <3.3.17` (GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8), reached by `vitest → vite → postcss (overridden) → nanoid@3.3.16`.
  - **⚠️ The interesting part is HOW it went red.** Last green run was `c656a0e0` (2026-08-07 17:14); first failure `07dfb133` (2026-08-08 10:25). **Every commit in that window was `docs(…)`** — a new advisory was published against an already-installed version, so the gate flipped with nothing in the repo changing. **"Duration is the diagnostic" does not cover this case**: the run is real (52 s), the result is genuine, and no diff explains it. A red `audit` that nobody introduced is the easiest kind to start ignoring.
  - **No production exposure — measured, not assumed.** `npm ls nanoid` in **`server/`** (the prod, internet-facing tree) returns **empty**; it exists only in the root tree via `vitest`, a devDependency.
  - **The fix is an `overrides` entry, per CLAUDE.md — NOT `npm audit fix`.** Root `package.json` already overrides `postcss` at `">=8.5.18"`, which resolves to 8.5.23 and still carries the vulnerable `nanoid`. ⚠️ **This is the recorded hazard in its exact form: an `overrides` pin can BECOME the vulnerability** — the `postcss` pin is doing its job and the transitive dependency underneath it moved. Add `"nanoid": ">=3.3.17"` and re-derive with `npm ls nanoid` **in both trees**. ⚠️ Regenerating `package-lock.json` requires `nvm use` first (npm 10, not 11) — see the Node-24 note in CLAUDE.md. *[severity: hygiene/gate-erosion · blocks: nothing · no prod exposure]*

- **C5 · Authz batch 2** — the residual cross-book authz holes Unit-0 book-scoping never adopted; read-only leaks + one write-adjacent gap. Fails safe on writes (reads leak info, not mutation):
  - **B1-F5** + **I12-R1** — read-only cross-book leaks: `admin.js` `GET /assignments/:book` (~`:986`) exposes another book's assignments/editor-names/progress; `GET /api/pipeline/jobs` + `/jobs/:jobId` expose every book's jobs. **I12-R1 is tracked as [issue #328](https://github.com/SigurdurVilhelmsson/namsbokasafn-efni/issues/328); INVESTIGATED 2026-07-25 (findings in the issue comment) — every claim verified against `main`, no line drift. ⚠️ The fix shape changed: `GET /jobs` has ZERO callers (all four client sites use `/jobs/:jobId`), so DELETE it rather than scope it** — the `apply-all` precedent; that removes the enumerate-every-book half outright instead of leaving a maintained dead endpoint. Then scope `/jobs/:jobId` on `job.book` vs `req.user.books` (mirror `requireRole.js:135`), **keep the ADMIN bypass** (`:119-121`), return **404 not 403**. Also noted: `req.query.book` is caller-controlled (targetable, not just default-open); jobs additionally leak `userId`; jobs are **in-memory only** (`pipelineService.js:38`) so exposure dies at restart. No test covers this — `§4c` (`a4-coverage.spec.js:166`) checks UI panel visibility by role, not API book-scope. **[LEAD 2026-07-25] queued for after C1d.**

## ⚒️ Post-run manual-fix ledger — anomalies deliberately NOT wired into the re-MT

**Established 2026-08-23 by [LEAD] ruling, alongside the §C88 Phase 1.2 decision.**

**What this section is for.** Some defects cost more to wire into the §C82 run than a human
costs to fix by hand afterwards. Deferring one is a legitimate call — **losing it is not.**
This is the ONE place a deferred-to-manual item is recorded, and it is the checklist runbook
**Phase 4.5** works through after the run and before either editor resumes.

**Admission rule — an item belongs here when ALL of these hold:**
1. It is in a **KEPT** book (`efnafraedi-2e`, `lifraen-efnafraedi`). Withdrawn books are §C109's,
   not this ledger's — **check before adding**: §C102 looks like a fit and is *physics-only*.
2. **The run will not fix it.** State WHY in the item. An anomaly the re-MT resolves on its own
   must NOT be listed — a ledger that lists self-healing items teaches people to ignore it.
3. Wiring it into the run costs materially more than the hand fix — **say what the code fix
   would have been**, so a later reader can re-take the trade instead of inheriting it blind.

🔴 **THE PROCESS RULE, and it is the point of the section:** when you defer something because
wiring it in costs more than a hand fix, **add it here in the SAME commit as the decision.**
A deferral recorded only in a session, a PR body or a spec is a deferral that will be lost — this
file's own § One source of truth exists because exactly that happened to eight findings.

✅ **COMPLETENESS — THE LIST IS NOW EMPTY. M0 subtracted it from three to one (2026-08-23), and M1 was CLOSED BY CODE on 2026-08-24 (PR #412).** ⚠️ **An empty ledger is not a discharged one** — the admission rule stands, and the next deferral goes here in the same commit as the decision.

**§C115**. **M0's range, predicate and stated exclusions are in the M0 entry below — read them

  - **The mechanism:** `m68727`'s `<media id="fs-idp1427264">` carries a 485-character alt containing a **raw, unescaped `>`** (`“Δ U > 0”` — while the `<` beside it IS escaped). Empty text ⇒ `addSegment` returns `null` (**M2**) *and* the structure's `alt` is `undefined` ⇒ `readAlt` returns `''` ⇒ published **`alt=""`** (**M3**).
  - 🔴 **WHY THE STRIKE MATTERS MORE THAN THE MERGE: the hand fix they prescribed CANNOT BE PERFORMED.** There is no segment, so the editor cannot reach it; `05-publication/` HTML is overwritten by the next render; and `01-source` is READ-ONLY and legally load-bearing, so escaping the `>` at source is forbidden. ▶ **A ledger item prescribing an impossible hand fix is worse than no item — it reads as discharged when the work cannot be done.** That is the failure M0 existed to catch, and it caught it in its own seed data.
  - 📌 **Severity is HIGHER than either item implied:** `alt=""` tells a screen reader *"decorative, skip"* — **strictly worse than English alt text**, which at least carries meaning. It is the only empty alt among **1,381** published `<img>` across both kept books.
  - → **§C115** owns it now. Evidence: [`test-results/m0-anomaly-sweep-2026-08-23.md`](../../test-results/m0-anomaly-sweep-2026-08-23.md)

## Provenance & sizing

- **Inventory basis:** a 6-agent extraction sweep (2026-07-21) over the pre-semester campaign register + the status dashboard + the SDD ledger + CLAUDE.md + memory, then controller dedup/consolidation. Raw 189 open findings → consolidated here; two already-resolved false-positives (B4-D11, I18-R1) excluded.
  - **⚠️ Known defect in that basis, found 2026-07-26 — every source listed above is a *derivative*.** The `docs/audit/` reports the campaigns were created to work down are **not** in the list, so this register tracks findings discovered *during* items but never the findings the work was chartered to fix. Measured consequence: `grep -c '2026-07-11-server-code-review'` over the predecessor campaign = **0**; `grep -oE 'Batch [A-H]'` = **1 of 8**. **8 review findings were carried by nothing** until the closure audit recovered them (now **C10**). **Rule for the next inventory sweep: include the primary audit documents, and disposition their findings by id — a batch-level "shipped" is not a finding-level disposition.**
- **Critical path:** P0 is the spine — until P0-1 (deploy) + P0-2 (vefur sync) run, the 21 shipped items and all content fixes are invisible to their users. The **[CODE]** backlog (P1–P3) does not gate delivery and can proceed in parallel with the LEAD lane, subject to the mid-QA deploy caveat.
- **First codeable pickups (recommended order):** C1 appendices (biggest coherent value, unblocks appendix editorial) → C2 Playwright-red (restores E2E trust) → C3 corpus/TM durability (cheap, closes a real durability lie) → then P2 batches by decision-readiness.
